newsitem.title: UK: FAGSA to raise international role at Geneva AGM.
newsitem.headline: FAGSA to raise international role at Geneva AGM.

text.p: Raising international awareness of the role of the Federation of Airline General Sales Agents (FAGSA) will be one of the key issues at its annual general meeting in Geneva next week, FAGSA Director Carlo Talei-Franzesi told Reuters in a telephone interview from Milan.
A cargo general sales agent runs the cargo and service department of an airline, but remains financially independent and is paid by results.
The organisation, which was formed in London in September 1995, will be holding its second AGM on November 5.

This will also coincide with the AGM being held by the International Air Transport Association(IATA) in Geneva on November 4 and 5 and allow talks to take place between airline management, IATA representatives and FAGSA members, he said.

"We want to have someone dedicated to representing us with international bodies. This is a very important area for us as we do not yet have international status," he told Reuters in a telephone interview from Milan.

"Airlines are our principals and freight forwarders our customers. That's why we want to start an ongoing dialogue with both IATA and the FIATA, which represents forwarders at an international level," he said.
"We are also looking for an improved relationship with the SITA," he added. SITA is a co-operatively held communications agency owned mainly by international airlines.
FAGSA already has a liaison bureau in Brussels to represent its interests with the European Commission's transport directorate, Talei-Franzesi said.
Next week's meeting is also expected to finalise details of a captive insurance company, owned by FAGSA members.
The new company is being established through London broker Willis Corroon Group Plc and is expected to be set up in the Channel Islands with an initial capital of stg 350,000, he said.
This will provide insurance cover for FAGSA members and thus reduce the financial burden of bank guarantees, required when representing airlines.

"The cost of bank guarantees to cover cargo revenues, airway bills etc. can be very high and they hit our cash flow... The new system will wipe out a lot of these costs. Even if the insurance commission costs the same as the bank guarantee, shareholders should get a share of any profit at the end of the year," he added.
"And if we have a good record, the insurance cost should go down rather than being a fixed commission from the banks," he said.
The creation of a small permanent secretariat and the need for improved training will also be discussed, Talei-Franzesi said.
"We are also looking for ways of following and exchanging more information on carriers and aviation developments worldwide, including use of the Internet," he added.

FAGSA has 73 members in 29 countries in 29 countries representing an aggregate of 657 airlines with a total turnover of US$1.7 billion, a statement by the organisation said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
